posts.body_html:
I've had Adrian slack for 2 years now, last year it was almost all green, with white lids. This year its giving me some nice color, after getting some fresh media. I've also found it to be one of my more vigorous plants, very first to wake up right as March began, and grows fairly fast. It went from a single growth point rhizome to a 7 growth point plant within a season.

I'm not sure what part of the country scryllarus grows in, but mine here in Georgia often opens up with similar colors to his and look exactly like that. Interestingly, as the pitchers color up in the sun, they often become much more white and look closer to Mike's.

Thes pitchers looked very similar to scryllarus' when they first opened (even with the pink top), now in June they look like this. You can see a fresh pitcher opening up and notice how much less colorful it is than the colored up pitchers.

posts.body_html:
Sorry for taking so long to respond, I haven't checked the forums in a fat minute. I live in Missouri (zone 5a), and my 'Adrian Slack' emerges anywhere from green to pink, then fades to white. What I noticed is that having a warm spring causes the pitchers to emerge green and a cold spring (like this year) causes the pitchers to emerge pinkish, like you saw in my previous photos. I'm not too sure on this though, as this is only my 2nd year owning the plant. Here's a summer pitcher, it should match more of what you're imagining when you think of 'Adrian Slack'
This is a newer pitcher

Hope this clears things up a bit!
